layers.title: MOLA elevation (hypsometric tint)
layers.credit: NASA/GSFC MGS MOLA Science Team; PDS Geosciences Node MEGDR (Smith et al. 2003)
layers.note: Display only: -8200 m (violet-blue) to +21300 m (white), metres above the MOLA areoid. Point values: read manifest.dem (mola_2880.i16.gz), same footprint, 1/8 degree.

layers.title: Geologic Map of Mars (USGS SIM 3292), unit raster
layers.mission: Multiple (Viking, MGS, Mars Odyssey, MRO, Mars Express data used by the map)
layers.instrument: Map compilation (THEMIS, MOLA, HRSC, CTX, HiRISE, Viking VIS); not an instrument product
layers.credit: Tanaka, K. L., Skinner, J. A. Jr., Dohm, J. M., Irwin, R. P. III, Kolb, E. J., Fortezzo, C. M., Platz, T., Michael, G. G., Hare, T. M. (2014), USGS SIM 3292
layers.note: Display raster rasterised at 2048x1024 (~0.18 deg) from the full-resolution polygons; for exact unit lookups use geology_global.json (simplified 0.03 deg). Colours are assigned by this pipeline (not USGS cartographic colours). Geologic units are interpretations at 1:20,000,000. valueFile is gzip (suffix .gz).

layers.title: Odyssey GRS water-equivalent hydrogen (Boynton et al. 2007)
layers.credit: W. V. Boynton et al. (2007), JGR 112, E12S99; PDS ODY-M-GRS-5-ELEMENTS-V1.0 (NASA PDS Geosciences Node)
layers.note: Smoothed 5x5 degree bins (10 degree boxcar), 1508 of 2592 bins have data; transparent = no data (high latitudes, where the GRS H signal needs a different model, are NOT covered). Resolution is ~300 km: it describes the regional upper ~1 m, never a site. Resampled bilinearly between valid bin centres for display. valueFile is gzip (suffix .gz). Display: YlGnBu 0..12 wt%.

layers.title: TES nighttime apparent thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon 2007)
layers.credit: N. E. Putzig & M. T. Mellon (2007), Icarus 191; PDS MGS-M-TES-5-TIMAP-V1.0 (NASA PDS Geosciences Node)
layers.note: Night map, 20 pixel/degree (~3 km), derived range 5..5000 tiu; transparent = not computed (poles beyond +/-87 deg, outside 5..5000). Apparent TI from a surface-temperature model, so higher = more rock/induration, lower = dust/sand. valueFile is gzip (suffix .gz). Display: inferno, log scale 25..1200.

layers.title: TES Dust Cover Index (Ruff & Christensen 2002), colourised
layers.credit: S. W. Ruff & P. R. Christensen (2002), JGR 107(E12), 5127; image via NASA/JPL Mars Trek "MGS TES, Global Dust"
layers.note: DISPLAY ONLY, no valueFile: Mars Trek and ASU serve only the colourised image (blue = more dust-covered, red = less dust, scale not published with the file), the DCI numbers are not on PDS/Trek, so no value is invented for point queries. Spectral index applies to dust thick enough to mask TIR spectra, 3.5 km pixels, coverage about +/-60..70 deg (black = no data -> transparent).

layers.title: Surface slope from the global MOLA DEM
layers.instrument: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), slope computed by this pipeline
layers.credit: Computed from NASA/GSFC MGS MOLA MEGDR; method: central differences on the 1/8 degree grid
layers.note: Baseline ~14.8 km (2 pixels of ~7.4 km): this is regional slope, NOT lander-scale slope; it cannot see rocks, scarps under ~km width or crater rims. valueFile is gzip (suffix .gz). Display: viridis 0..20 deg.
